problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-x(t)+2y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-2x(t)+4y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives an equation of the line in the phase space that contains all equilibrium points of the system above?
worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$

The equilibrium (fixed) points of a system ${x}^{′}(t)=f(x,y)$ are the points for which $f(x,y)=0.$ So, we get the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-x+2y=0 \\ -2x+4y=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the second equation is a multiple of the first one. So, we can disregard the second equation. 

From the first equation, we get

$$
-x+2y=0\,⇒\,2y=x\,⇒\,y=\frac{x}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the equilibrium points are given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}k \\ \frac{k}{2}\end{aligned}],\,k\in R.
$$

This determines the line with the equation $y=\frac{x}{2}.$
